name: Unauthorized Access Detection System
tagline: A full-stack vision pipeline that recognizes faces and guards identity in real time

scenes.title: Watches, Recognizes & Reacts — In Real Time
scenes.body: A full-stack, vision-based access-control system: a FastAPI backend wraps the detection/recognition pipeline, a TanStack Start web dashboard gives security staff live multi-camera monitoring, and a companion Expo mobile app pushes alerts straight to a phone — all sharing one JWT-secured API contract.
scenes.imageAlt: UAD pipeline flow: cameras, preprocess, YOLOv8n, IoU tracking, SCRFD, alignment, ArcFace

scenes.title: Two Detectors Running in Parallel
scenes.body: SCRFD scans every frame for faces while YOLOv8n tracks full-body positions with a custom IoU tracker — running side by side instead of one feeding the other. Overlapping face detections are collapsed with NMS and a min-area filter before anything reaches recognition.
scenes.imageAlt: Overlapping detection boxes filtered down to one via NMS + Min Filter

scenes.title: Every Face Gets Straightened Before It's Compared
scenes.body: SCRFD returns five facial landmarks per detection — eyes, nose, mouth corners. A similarity transform warps each crop to a canonical 112×112 frame before it ever reaches ArcFace, so a tilted head or an off-angle camera doesn't throw off the match.
scenes.imageAlt: Rotated face mesh warped and cropped to an aligned bounding frame

scenes.title: One Identity, Averaged From Many Faces
scenes.body: Enrolling someone runs a handful of their reference photos through the same SCRFD → align → ArcFace path, then averages the resulting 512-dimension vectors into one signature per identity. A live face is accepted only above a 0.817 cosine-similarity threshold against that signature.
scenes.imageAlt: Three enrolled face embeddings averaged into a single 512-dimension vector array

scenes.title: One Face Can't Borrow Another Body's Identity
scenes.body: Faces are matched to body tracks one-to-one, only within the top zone of a person's bounding box, and an identity already claimed by another track can't be reassigned. Identified tracks are re-verified every 2 seconds so a spoofed match can't persist.
scenes.imageAlt: Two independent body tracks with track IDs, and a YOLOv8-offline face-only fallback notice

scenes.title: From Detection to a Persisted, Audited Alert
scenes.body: A per-track state machine — FRESH → ACTIVE → IDENTIFIED / UNAUTHORIZED — fires an alert after 2 seconds of confirmed unauthorized presence, with a 30-second cooldown to avoid flooding. Every alert carries an encrypted snapshot, persists to Postgres + pgvector, and is written to an audit trail — exportable as CSV/PDF and pushed live over WebSocket.
scenes.imageAlt: Camera view of a recognized person tagged AUTHORIZED with ID, status and access level

scenes.title: A Dashboard for the Wall, an App for the Pocket
scenes.body: The same JWT-secured API backs a TanStack Start (React 19) dashboard with live camera grids and alert-throughput charts, and an Expo/React Native app that pushes alerts straight to a guard's phone. It all ships behind Docker Compose and a Caddy reverse proxy with automatic TLS, no exposed database port, and 35 tests — 13 pipeline, 22 API — that run without a GPU.

name: ClinicHub
tagline: A multi-tenant booking & subscription platform for clinics and medical centers

scenes.title: One Backend, Three Kinds of Tenants
scenes.body: A Laravel 12 API serving clinics, medical centers, and their patients from one codebase — subscription billing, appointment booking, and WhatsApp notifications behind a single JWT-protected contract.

scenes.title: Refresh Tokens, Rotated on Every Use
scenes.body: Short-lived JWT access tokens (15 min) pair with HMAC-SHA256-hashed refresh tokens that rotate on every use and chain through a replaced_by_token_hash trail — so a stolen refresh token gets caught the moment the real user refreshes next.

scenes.title: Every Login Is a Trackable Device
scenes.body: Each session carries a device_id, platform, FCM token, and server-resolved IP geolocation — letting a user see "Chrome on Windows · Erbil, Iraq · 2 days ago" and remotely terminate it, or an admin block a specific device outright.

scenes.title: Plans, Entitlements & Trial Periods
scenes.body: Clinics and medical centers subscribe to tiered plans with JSON-encoded entitlements — max patients per month, secretary seats, clinic counts — enforced per-request instead of hardcoded per plan name.

scenes.title: Appointment Reminders Land on WhatsApp
scenes.body: An Evolution API integration sends booking confirmations and reminders straight to a patient's WhatsApp, alongside Firebase push notifications for the native apps — because email reminders mostly go unread.

scenes.title: A Live Swagger Contract, Not a Stale Postman Doc
scenes.body: Every endpoint is annotated for l5-swagger, so the OpenAPI spec regenerates straight from the code — while a hand-written Postman quick-reference in Arabic covers the common flows for the rest of the team.

name: Load-Tested Commerce Engine
tagline: A NestJS commerce backend built to survive load, not just pass a demo

scenes.title: Built to Get Load-Tested, Not Just Demoed
scenes.body: A NestJS + PostgreSQL commerce backend with a k6 test suite covering eight named non-functional requirements — race conditions, rate limits, async queues, batch jobs, load distribution — run against the real Docker Compose stack, not mocks.

scenes.title: 50 Concurrent Buyers, Exactly One Order
scenes.body: NFR-1 spins up 50 virtual users who all try to buy the last unit of the same product at once. A pessimistic lock at the database layer guarantees exactly one order succeeds and zero requests 500 — verified automatically, not just claimed.

scenes.title: Emails and PDFs Happen Off the Request Path
scenes.body: BullMQ + Redis move invoice generation (PDFKit) and order-confirmation emails (Nodemailer) into background jobs, so a checkout request returns fast instead of waiting on a mail server or a PDF renderer.

scenes.title: Prometheus Metrics, Structured Logs, Health Checks
scenes.body: prom-client exposes request-level metrics for Prometheus/Grafana, Winston writes daily-rotated structured logs, and a dedicated health module reports readiness — the observability stack you'd actually want on call for this.

scenes.title: It Watches Its Own Containers and Scales Itself
scenes.body: A small Node script polls docker stats every 15 seconds and scales the app service between 3 and 8 replicas behind nginx based on live CPU/RAM thresholds — with a cooldown so it doesn't thrash under bursty traffic.

scenes.title: React 19, TanStack Query & Zod on the Client
scenes.body: The storefront is a separate React 19 + TypeScript app: TanStack Query for server state, React Hook Form + Zod for validated checkout forms, and Axios wired to the same JWT contract the backend's k6 suite tests against.

name: MiniNN
tagline: A neural network library built from raw NumPy, no autograd framework underneath

scenes.title: Backprop, Written by Hand
scenes.body: MiniNN is a from-scratch neural network library in pure NumPy. Every forward pass, gradient, and optimizer update is code I wrote, not a call into PyTorch or TensorFlow.

scenes.title: Dense, Dropout, and Batch Norm — All Hand-Derived
scenes.body: Dense layers use He/Xavier initialization. BatchNormalization tracks running statistics for inference. Dropout, ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh, and Softmax Cross-Entropy round out a small but complete layer library.

scenes.title: SGD, Momentum, AdaGrad, and Adam
scenes.body: Each optimizer tracks per-parameter state keyed by Python's id(), so the same parameter tensor is recognized correctly across layers even when two layers happen to share a name.

scenes.title: Mini-Batches, Validation Metrics, Grid Search
scenes.body: A Trainer class handles mini-batch gradient descent with train/validation tracking, and a HyperparameterTuner runs grid search over learning rates and layer sizes — the scaffolding every deep learning framework needs underneath the math.

scenes.title: 784 → 256 → 128 → 10, No Shortcuts
scenes.body: The same library trains a 2D toy classifier, the Iris dataset, and a batch-normalized MNIST digit classifier — the exact numbers a framework needs to get right to be trustworthy, not just one cherry-picked demo.

name: School Management System
tagline: A REST API for running an entire school's day-to-day operations

scenes.title: Every Part of Running a School, One API
scenes.body: An Express + PostgreSQL backend covering students, teachers, classes, exams, attendance, tuition, and notifications — over 30 controllers, models, and services deep, backed by 37 versioned migrations.

scenes.title: Years, Semesters, Subjects, Curricula
scenes.body: Academic years contain semesters, semesters map to curricula, and curricula assign subjects to classes — a real hierarchy, not a flat "course" table, so a student's schedule resolves correctly across years.

scenes.title: Questions, Attempts, Answers, Grades
scenes.body: Exams are built from a question bank, students submit exam_attempts, individual answers are recorded and graded, and the result rolls up into the student's academic record automatically.

scenes.title: Two Attendance Systems, One Pattern
scenes.body: Students and employees are tracked through separate attendance tables with the same reporting shape, so the same dashboards and export logic serve both without special-casing.

scenes.title: Payments That Actually Reconcile
scenes.body: Tuition payments are tracked per student with status transitions, so office staff can see who's paid, who's overdue, and export the numbers without cross-referencing a spreadsheet.

scenes.title: An Excel Sheet Becomes 200 Student Records
scenes.body: xlsx-powered bulk upload lets office staff import a whole class roster from a spreadsheet in one request, instead of typing every student in by hand.

scenes.title: The Right Notification to the Right Role
scenes.body: Firebase Cloud Messaging tokens are tied to roles and permissions, so a grade update notifies a parent, an attendance flag notifies a homeroom teacher, and neither gets the other's noise.
